info.name: Gig Lanka API
info.description:
Covers the Sprint 0 auth endpoints (§5), the Sprint 1 profile endpoints (§8), the Sprint 1 gig endpoints (§10), the Sprint 1 application endpoints (§11.7–§11.11) and the Sprint 2 business-side application endpoints (§11.12–§11.17, GL-219) defined in docs/api-contract.md. Set baseUrl to point at a running server; accessToken/refreshToken are populated automatically by the Register/Login/Refresh requests.

Profiles folder — run in order. 'Register seeker' and 'Register business' each store their own token (seekerToken/businessToken) and user id (seekerUserId/businessUserId), so the refusal requests can act as one role against the other without re-logging in.

Gigs folder — run in order. Setup requests register an owning business, an intruding business and a seeker, then Create requests store gigId (kept open throughout) and gigCloseId (closed partway through) so the ownership, ownership-vs-existence and closed-visibility requests below all act on real ids.

Reviews folder — run in order, after running `npm run seed` against the target database and pasting the printed hired-application id into the `hiredApplicationId` variable. Setup requests log in as the seeded seeker/business and register a stranger, so the party, non-party, category and duplicate checks below all act on the real seeded hire.

Applications folder — run in order. Setup requests register an owning business and a seeker, then create an open gig (appGigId) and a second gig closed partway through (appGigCloseId). The apply/list/read requests below build and consume appId. The withdraw-after-hire check reuses the seeded hire from the Reviews folder (`npm run seed` + hiredApplicationId), with its own login step so this folder can run independently of Reviews.

item.name: Reviews
item.description:
GL-195/196/197 review endpoints — see §12 of docs/api-contract.md. Hiring doesn't exist in the product until Sprint 2, so these run against the hire seeded by `npm run seed` (server/scripts/seed.js prints the seeded application's id on each run).

Before running this folder: run `npm run seed` against the target server's database, then paste the printed application id into the `hiredApplicationId` collection variable. Run top to bottom — the two Setup requests log in as the seeded seeker/business and a fresh stranger, storing the tokens and ids everything below uses. Safe to re-run: the create requests accept 201 or 409 (already reviewed).

Not covered here: the not-hired 409 path (APPLICATION_NOT_HIRED). Nothing in the product can currently produce a non-Hired application to call this endpoint against, so that path is verified by the automated suite instead (server/tests/integration/review.create.test.js), not by a request in this collection.

Applications
item.description:
GL-182/183/184 application endpoints — see §11.7–§11.10 of docs/api-contract.md. Run top to bottom: Setup registers an owning business, the applicant seeker and a second seeker (for the wrong-party checks), then creates an open gig (appGigId, stays open for most of the folder) and a second gig (appGigCloseId, closed partway through for the GIG_CLOSED check).

The withdraw-after-hire check at the end needs `npm run seed` run against the target database first, with the printed hired application id pasted into `hiredApplicationId` (same precondition as the Reviews folder) — it logs in as the seeded seeker itself, so it doesn't depend on the Reviews folder having run.

GL-252/253 business-side endpoints (§11.12–§11.17) continue below. The second seeker (appOtherSeekerToken, otherwise only used for wrong-party checks) applies to appGigId to give the two lists and the view/shortlist/hire chain something to act on (appTransitionId); a third seeker (appRejectSeekerToken) applies separately so the four rejection-refusal checks and the success case (appRejectId) don't collide with the hire chain. The 'other business' refusal checks reuse `gigOtherBusinessToken` from the Gigs folder, so this section depends on the Gigs folder having run first in the same collection run.
